source.value:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}  = 2xy - x^2 - y^2.
$$

Using a substitution of the form $z= x - y,$ transform the differential equation into an equation of the form $z'(x) = f(z).$ What is the function $f(z)?$

source.question: e-9036
source.value:
First, we factor the right-hand side of the given equation, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-(x-y)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we make the substitution

$$
z = x - y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x} = 1 - \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} \quad \Longrightarrow\quad
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} =  1 - \dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x}.
$$

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =-{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing this equation in the form $z'(x) = f(z),$ we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x}  =  z^2 + 1.
$$

Therefore, $f(z) = z^2 + 1.$

source.value:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x}  = \dfrac{1 - x - y}{x + y}.
$$

The general solution to this equation can be expressed in the form

$$
g(x,y) = 2x + C,
$$

where $C$ is a constant. What is $g(x,y)?$

source.question: e-9038
source.value:
First, we factor the right-hand side of the given equation.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1-(x+y)}{x+y}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we make the substitution

$$
z = x+y.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x} = 1 + \dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\dfrac{\textrm{d}y}{\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x} - 1.
$$

Therefore, the original equation can be written in terms of $z$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-1 & =\frac{1-z}{z}\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing this equation in the form $z'(x) = f(z)$ gives

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}z}{\textrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{z}.
$$

This differential equation is separable. So, we separate the variables and integrate both sides with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}z\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x} & =1 \\ \int z\,\text{d}z & =\int \text{d}x \\ \frac{{z}^{2}}{2} & =x+K \\ {z}^{2} & =2x+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C = 2K.$

Finally, we write the equation in terms of $y$ and $x$ using our original substitution, as follows:

$$
(x+y)^2 = 2x + C
$$

Therefore, 

$$
g(x,y) = (x+y)^2.
$$
